author: c2-sql-edu-critic (independent education critic subagent, fresh context, read-only; reviewed commit 8a7daa17)

findings.claim: §12 (feedback on every option), wrong teaching, one item: In "o1 two rows, named columns", the feedback on the second option says "VALUES appears once, and this form also omits the column list." That option, INSERT INTO pets (pet_id, name) VALUES (1, 'Rex') VALUES (2, 'Mia');, does name its column list. A learner who checks the option against its feedback is told something false about the very thing the objective teaches (naming the columns).
findings.recommendation: Rewrite that feedback so it names only the real fault, for example: "Not quite. VALUES appears once; put a comma between the bracketed rows instead of a second VALUES."

findings.claim: E1/F5: The Problems panel files ordinary SQL mistakes under the label "Not in this practice editor": a typo ("SELEC * FROM students;"), a missing comma between two VALUES rows and a missing semicolon all show that label, and so does the untouched starter ("Write at least one SQL statement, ending with a semicolon"), before the first Run. Reproduced on all eight pages of the module: a missing semicolon at the end of line 3 (SELECT name / FROM students / WHERE city = 'Leeds' / SELECT 2;) shows "Ln 4 Not in this practice editor ... could not read the statement near select". The editor's own limits list says the label means "a limit of this page, not a sign that your SQL is wrong", so a beginner whose SQL is wrong is told it may be fine. On this page the most likely beginner slip, leaving out the comma between the two bracketed rows (which is exactly what Activity 2 practises), is filed under that label.
findings.recommendation: In page-build/controller.js, where EDITOR.kindLabels maps the adapter's limit kind to "Not in this practice editor", show parse problems under their own learner label, such as "Check your SQL", and keep "Not in this practice editor" for genuine subset limits (WITH, COPY, CREATE TABLE). If the adapter cannot tell the two apart, reword the matching LIMITS sentence in page-build/build.mjs so it no longer says the label is never a sign of wrong SQL.

findings.claim: C2: The retry question is about students ("Femi (student 6) now uses femi.o@example.com"). Its options name Chen and Leeds, and its explanations depend on the unique email rule and on which students live in Leeds. When the retry appears, the reading column shows only the enrollments table; the students table is in Activities 2 and 3, which are hidden.
findings.recommendation: Add the students table, with the email column and the note that email is unique, to Activity 4's reading column, or rewrite the retry on enrollments so the data it needs is already visible.

findings.claim: C1/C4: The task asks for a multi-row INSERT that names four columns and puts NULL in one row, but the only worked example is a single-row INSERT into instructors. The several-rows form and an unquoted NULL inside VALUES appear only in prose; hint 2 supplies the NULL. The example also inserts into lead_id, a column of a table this page never shows or explains.
findings.recommendation: Make the reading-column example show the exact shape: two bracketed rows separated by a comma, one with NULL, on a table the page shows, such as courses with fee NULL. Use different values from the task so it is not copied, and drop lead_id or say what it is in a clause.

findings.claim: E5 (practice-feedback-policy 1.3): Parse problems point at the line after the mistake, not at the line to change. A missing comma at the end of line 2 of a multi-row INSERT is reported as "Ln 3 ... near "("", and a missing semicolon at the end of line 4 is reported as "Ln 5 ... near "select"", which is the policy's own counter-example. Reproduced on all eight pages: a missing semicolon at the end of line 3 is reported at Ln 4. The message does not say that the place to look is the end of the line before. Seen on this page in Activity 2.
findings.recommendation: Where the adapter reports "could not read the statement near" on the first token of a line, have the page controller (page-build/controller.js) add "Check the end of the line before it too, for a missing comma or semicolon", or point the Ln marker at the previous non-blank line. The adapter is copied unchanged, so the wording fix belongs in this module's controller unless a new adapter version changes the location.

findings.claim: E3 (policy 1.1): Activity 3 shows the near-miss verdict "Almost." when two checks are missing: an UPDATE with no preview SELECT and no RETURNING got "Almost." followed by two instructions. A near-miss is right in substance and differs in one named detail.
findings.recommendation: In page-build/src/insert-update-and-delete.topic.js, set near only when exactly one of preview or RETURNING is missing.

findings.claim: D2: Objective o2 says "Write UPDATE and DELETE statements…", but the learner never types a DELETE. DELETE appears only as options in the Activity 4 choice.
findings.recommendation: Either add a DELETE line to an editor task (for example, remove a cancelled enrollment after previewing it), or reword o2 so writing is promised only for UPDATE and DELETE is recognised.

findings.claim: A4: The In interviews row (what happens when an UPDATE or DELETE has no WHERE clause) matches Activity 1 exactly, but the page does not say so. On inner-and-left-joins and anti-joins-and-self-joins the row ends "this activity practises that choice" / "exactly that shape".
findings.recommendation: End the row with a pointer such as "Activity 1 practises exactly this", as the two join pages do.

findings.claim: F5/B5: One editor has three names and two verdicts. Output opens with "(lesson simulator, not real PostgreSQL server)", the bar says "Practice editor: follows PostgreSQL on this page's sample tables", the status line says "SQL practice editor", and after a run that stops with a PostgreSQL ERROR the Problems tab still says "No problems found by the lesson checker".
findings.recommendation: Use one name everywhere, such as "practice editor". The "not real" tail of the Output header comes from EDITOR.language = 'PostgreSQL server' in page-build/controller.js, and its "lesson simulator" prefix and the Problems sentence come from the shared shell. Change the page-owned part now; ask for a shell version that, after an ERROR, says "No problems before Run; see Output for the ERROR" and drops "not real".

findings.claim: B5: Shared controller and build wording. (1) Confidence choices read Low / Medium / High; DESIGN.md "Assessment: options, confidence, feedback" sets "Guessing", "Fairly sure", "Certain". (2) A wrong prediction opens "Your guess was not this time; the right answer is marked.", which drops a word. (3) The end-of-page message reads "Activity 2 and 3 and 4 are not done yet".
findings.recommendation: In page-build/build.mjs (CONF) use Guessing / Fairly sure / Certain. In page-build/controller.js write "Your guess was not right this time; the right answer is marked." and join several open activities as "Activities 2, 3 and 4 are not done yet".

findings.claim: G7/F1: On a headless Chromium 570 x 1000 viewport, opening the page from file:// leaves it scrolled 157 px down with the hash #activity-1. The topic title, progress line and Topic objectives are above the first screen, which starts at the lesson-path row. At 1280 px the scroll was 0 on seven pages and 121 px on inner-and-left-joins. This was measured only under file:// in headless Chromium, and the cause was not found: history.replaceState did not throw when called after load, and turning off scroll anchoring did not change the result.
findings.recommendation: Check this in a desktop browser and in the platform embed. If it reproduces, do not set location.hash on first load (restore scroll to 0, or skip the hash when there is none), so the first screen shows the title and Topic objectives.
